c-0: ^Margaret: How blunt, I like that. This is not something you should be shameful about. It was your determination to leave your parents alone that brought you all the way here, and you don't need to perform that hypocritical justice.

^(You look at the screen. There's still around one hour and a half for decision making. But you have waited for this moment for so long. It was that thrilling excitement that keeps you from pushing the change.)

b: ^But all of a sudden, you feel that all this while you've been persuading yourself to perform an identity.
^(Margaret looking into your eyes with that professional half-smile. You shiver as you realize how she looks different from how you perceive yourself.)

^(When you were a student, every morning before you set off to school, you will look yourself closely in the mirror. During those tough years when you first moved to the city, you always have a sense of inferiority, so at least you will make yourself decent enough among your peers.)

^(You deliberately erase the naviety on your face, day by day, and now, when you finally feel yourself grown up, standing just outside the threshold of adulthood, waiting for your coming-of-age ceremony in the form of a career promotion - You finally feel that something is wrong.)

Choice1: ^(Luckily, you still have a chance to revert it all back.)

s: ^Crash the code, and save the darkness.
^Don't mind the intrusive thoughts. Be yourself.

c-0: ^Margaret: If you can eliminate things that are meaningful to others, why would you preserve something meaningful to you?

s: ^If losing the last piece of night from the city, the only piece of me remaining in the city will be gone.
^I would never hesitate anymore. I will press the button.

c-0: ^(You reached Light City late in the night. When the train ringed the bell and left for the next destination, passengers went down from the platform, their back view blend into the light in the station... At the age of 15, you had a strong impulse to stay.)

^(The soft glow in the station is close within a reach, but you hesitated to enter. The station is like a "light hole" where no darkness can escape, nor things related to darkness - the loneliness, nostalgia, solitude.)

^(You stepped back from the edge. You sat at the bench beside the rail. Summer breeze gently stroked your face. You suddenly miss home so much. The station shared the same stars with River Ville. That was 11:59PM, just before the last bus to the city set off.)

PreserveWinter: ^Margaret: (Chuckling) You are always like this. Say one thing and mean another.

b: ^(She looks into your eyes, silently. Through that scrutiny you slowly recall everything that you once sacrificed everything to escape from yet always revisited: River Ville, the train station, your old friend, old dream, and the nights.)
^(And you ask yourself a question: If something evil ever happens in your Light City, just in that deserted train station you deliberately preserve, will you be guilty for that?

c-1: ^But does that established vision really worth your sacrifice? Standing just before a new beginning, should it be a turning point for your new life?

PreserveWinter: ^She never responds back. As though she does not have an answer.
^You have so many similar moments in the past of your life, standing at the crossroads and thinking whether ten years later you will be regretted for any of your choice today.
^But you never know. You just never know.

Ending0: ^You reversed that decision in one second. As your cursor almost clicks the submit button, a sudden impulse stopped you from doing that.
^All this time your life has been following a routine, and you never consider to change.
^But you started with that minor rebellion, and you will have more to come.
^One day you might spare some time to visit the station, and realize the world never collapse for a single piece of darkness.
^And you will exclaim: How beautiful the starry sky is!
Ending1: ^You pressed the button. You have done this for a thousand times. Approve forms, check implementation, this is just one of the many, and it does not make a difference.
^Or...It does make a difference. You soon received the notice of promotion. You stepped on the stage amid thunderous applause.

b: ^It is just another success in your life. You have earned yourself a decent life you deserve. Now, go enjoy your life that your parents never managed to see - this is the reason why they sent you here with no regret. You did not disappoint those who loved you. Congratulations!

^You definitely have given up something in order to stand here - but you made it. You might be regretted one day, but that's totally a matter of future. Now it's a matter of fact - you contended with a deeper desire, and finally got through. You will start from here, and look forward to a new life ahead.

Ending2: ^Despite all your time and effort, you gave up at the last minute. Not because you are afraid, but for your sudden memory of that starry sky. Tomorrow is the beginning of new year, after two days rest, you will continue your busy career life.
^Maybe just in these two days, you will pay a visit to that place of your memory, just for that long-lost starry sky.
Ending3: ^You once saw the consequences of uncovered surveillance, yet when the time comes, you chose to preserve the nights.
^You always know that the world is a vessel of humanity of different colors, including the shadowy ones. Still, you want to preserve that colorful nature, even the shadowy part.
^It is only with the contrast of darkness that you see the stars in the sky.
Ending4: ^You once dreamt of a city of light that eliminate all evils - and now your dream has been achieved.
^But you soon realize: a city of full surveillance does not eliminate the shadows hidden in the hearts.

^When the first incidence of deliberate murder happened in the Helio energy centre, using the light source as the weapon to torture the victim, you felt something was tore apart - an old dream has collapsed in its purpose, yet a new one never rises.
^That was the year you decided to join the Light Knights as a technical consultant, where you will not only study light, but become the light.
Ending5: ^The new year means an end and a new beginning: you quitted from your current position, as you know there is something more important in your life.

b: ^First thing first, you have to find Patty. You sent her a message, had a small chat with her, and kind of catch up: she has gotten married recently in River Ville, and is currently working as a teacher in the town school.

^She is the consultant for the exchange program you have gotten into, but with far more follow-up: She knows you've gone through a hard time when heading to Light City alone, so she provided follow-up consulting services for selected student.
^She missed you, but was afraid to disturb you, until you sent that message saying that you would like to visit her in River Ville.

^She talked incessantly about the development in River Ville, the new restaurants, and the tourist attractions built by the riverside. She promised she will bring you everywhere, tell you everything that you once missed but now intend to recollect.

^With your current savings, you are going to travel around the world. You are not necessarily sure if Star City will be a great place to live, but definitely, you will sit down at a streetside stall to have some chicken rice.
^At the age of 30, you finally realize, your old friend Bernard has never left. He was just waiting for you rewrite your stories.

^You will write some stories along the way. Perhaps you will publish the short novels as a collection: For Bernard, and do not explain to anyone who is Bernard. Shhh...This is a secret between you and Bernard.

^You finally realize that your true passion is about the process of research rather than the outcome of light. You might go back to school, or join an institute for scientific research. You won't be addressed as a professional engineer that make stuff come true, but a scientist that explores the ultimate theories of the world.

^But one day you will go back to your normal life. You might find a new job, something that fits you better. With the transforming space and time, you will eventually know your passion - or, find fun in routines. That is how life goes.

Ending6: ^You made a last minute change in your decision. Fix is pushed, you received the honor that you deserve.

^Fatigue swallows you like a dark fog creeping in. You are so resistant to change, which led to your decision to complete the job as normal; but you are also afraid of your current life like a gradually sinking ship.

^You moved to Star City, where stars can never be seen. Nothing is really different from Light City. You rent a new little apartment, facing the river, but that ideal life doesn't save you from meaninglessness. You had chicken rice for two months until you never want to see this dish again. You take 10PM instant noodles and coffee for your work.
